# Sources — `counsel:attorney-review-and-release`

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-sources.py from sources/*.toml. Do not edit. -->

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## ABA Formal Opinion 512 — Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools

American Bar Association, Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.americanbar.org/content/dam/aba/administrative/professional_responsibility/ethics-opinions/aba-formal-opinion-512.pdf>

**Authoritative for:** The national ethics framework for a lawyer's use of generative AI (July 29, 2024): competence, confidentiality and informed consent before client information enters a self-learning tool, communication with the client, candor, supervision, and what may reasonably be charged for AI-assisted work. Persuasive in New Jersey; the Supreme Court's own guidance governs.

## New Jersey Rules of Court, including the Rules of Professional Conduct

New Jersey Judiciary · NJ · public domain — quote freely

<https://www.njcourts.gov/attorneys/rules-of-court>

**Authoritative for:** The court rules that set the practice's clocks and duties — R. 1:3-1 (computing time), R. 1:21-6 (attorney trust and business accounts and their records), R. 1:21-7 (contingent fees), R. 4:80-6 (notice of probate and proof of mailing), R. 4:85-1 and 4:85-2 (the will-contest window) — and the Rules of Professional Conduct, which are an appendix to Part I: RPC 1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 1.14, 1.15, 5.1, 5.3, 5.4, 7.1 through 7.4. Amended annually by the Supreme Court's omnibus order, ordinarily effective September 1.

## New Jersey Statutes — current text

New Jersey Legislature, Office of Legislative Services · NJ · public domain — quote freely

<https://lis.njleg.state.nj.us/nxt/gateway.dll?f=templates&fn=default.htm>

Machine-readable: <https://pub.njleg.state.nj.us/statutes/>

**Authoritative for:** The current text of every New Jersey statute cited here — Title 3B (wills, probate, intestacy, fiduciary commissions, refunding bonds, the Uniform Trust Code), Title 46 (powers of attorney, the realty transfer fee and the Graduated Percent Fee), Title 26 (advance directives), Title 54 (the transfer inheritance tax and the bulk sale notice) and Title 52 (remote notarial acts). Read the section; a summary on a firm's website is not the law.

## Notice — Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence and Related Technologies: Benefits of AI Policies, Sample Starter Template

Supreme Court of New Jersey · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.njcourts.gov/notices/notice-responsible-use-of-artificial-intelligence-ai-and-related-technologies-benefits-of>

**Authoritative for:** The Supreme Court's model firm policy (March 2026): choose one confidentiality rule for AI tools, require lawyer review of every AI-assisted work product before it reaches a client, opposing counsel or the court, verify every citation against an official source or remove it, and check each tool's sharing, retention and training settings before use, including AI features built into everyday platforms.

## Preliminary Guidelines on the Use of Artificial Intelligence by New Jersey Lawyers

Supreme Court of New Jersey, Committee on Artificial Intelligence and the Courts · NJ · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.njcourts.gov/notices/notice-legal-practice-preliminary-guidelines-use-of-artificial-intelligence-new-jersey>

**Authoritative for:** How the Rules of Professional Conduct apply to a lawyer's use of AI (issued January 25, 2024, effective immediately): the duty to verify AI output, confidentiality before any client information enters a tool, candor, and supervision of staff and tools under RPC 5.1 to 5.3. The guidelines impose no new duty; they say which existing ones AI engages.
